ratings_why.fun: Three paths that all pour into one vain giant, with a board you shrink on purpose, make a draft you'd happily take; three keywords plus Champion is a lot to learn at once.
ratings_why.distinct: Gaps as fuel and Proud as a visible chequerboard use Bramble's fixed slots like no current tribe; Duel itself reads like a familiar pre-combat strike.

verdict_why: The fantasy and shape are there; a few rules a player can't yet read (Proud with Created units, Cork-Pop against Hartmut's cap, Gottfried's percentages) need one pass of wording.

points.text: With Sir Hartmut, it's unclear whether Master of the Cork-Pop's second trigger spends one of Hartmut's 'Twice a fight' uses. Say so on one of the two cards.
Proud doesn't say whether a Created unit beside it (a Bird Egg, a summon mid-fight) breaks it. Since the whole court depends on it, the keyword text should settle it.
Sir Gottfried's '+50% of his stats for each empty slot' could read as compounding. Write it as 'gains +50% of his starting stats per empty slot' or show the x4 at six gaps.
The Chronicler crossing out a name each spring is the tribe's best flavour beat. A 'you may' version keeps it and avoids feel-bad losses, as the designer suggests.
Refectory Prior's '4 or fewer units' is true for everyone early, so it reads as plain gold, not austerity. '3 or fewer' would tie it to the shrinking order.

standouts.why: The Chronicler turns 'splendid decline' into a turn rhythm: buy a fat unit, watch it be crossed out into the Champion.
Sir Hartmut, too lost in his song to stop, Duels on after each win; the card is the character.
Elder of the Centre pays the Champion for every empty slot, one plain line that makes gaps a choice you can see.

weakest.why: Refectory Prior is generic economy with a condition everyone meets early.
Sprucehold Envoy is a stock Discover with little lek in what it does.
Pennon-Squire is a plain keyword-and-stats giver; it reads fine but says nothing about knights.

flags.note: Herald of the Last Dawn with Grand Master Ottokar and Cork-Pop could clear a front row before anyone attacks.
Sir Gottfried at x4 (x7 golden) on a fed Champion, on purpose; worth the owner's eye.
How Master of the Cork-Pop's doubled triggers count against 'Twice a fight' limits isn't said.
